title: Impact analysis
description: The validated artifact specs/0001 R4 requires impact analysis to produce: a verdict from the closed set none | update | create, naming every implicated artifact by identifier. The named consumer is the thin-path orchestrator (scripts/orchestrate.py), which reads `verdict` to choose the transition out of the impact-analysis phase; the named producer is whatever performed the analysis. This artifact carries control flow, so .claude/rules/contracts.md requires this versioned schema and boundary validation before consumption. R4 fixes the content of this contract, which is why it exists before a dedicated producing agent does — spec 0001 states each artifact's schema arrives with the phase that produces it, and that phase arrives with the thin path. What this contract deliberately does not carry: any escalation threshold. specs/0001 R10 forbids inventing one ahead of executed workflows, and docs/bootstrap.md stage 5 holds it.

contract_version.description: A consumer rejects an artifact it was not built to read rather than inferring version from shape.

analysis_id.description: Stable identifier for this analysis, required for traceability by .claude/rules/contracts.md.

request_id.description: The change request this analysis classifies. specs/0001 R1: no phase runs without a change request, so an analysis that names none is not traceable to a reason for existing.

producer.description: What performed the analysis. Not a const: unlike concept-authoring-result/1, this contract is not owned by one named agent — R4 requires the artifact, not a particular producer of it.

verdict.description: The closed set fixed by specs/0001 R4. This is the field the orchestrator looks up to choose its transition, which is what keeps the choice a table read rather than an interpretation (R5). `none` still runs to acceptance: R3 requires the phase to run for every request, and acceptance evaluates closure over the observed diff regardless (R17, R18).

implicated.description: Every artifact this change implicates, by identifier. R4 requires knowledge objects and ADRs to be named; `concept` is admitted because the concept bundle is the knowledge layer the only existing producer operates on. Identifiers rather than content: restating an artifact here would put a second copy of it in a temporary file (specs/0001 R16 applies the same rule to the specification delta).

id.description: The artifact's own identifier, as that artifact declares it.

kind.description: Which class the identifier belongs to, so a consumer resolves it against the right contract.

then.description: A verdict that permanent knowledge must change, naming nothing it changes, is a verdict with nothing behind it. A `none` verdict may legitimately implicate nothing.
